chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who plays with his wife while he is in ihram until he ejaculates without sexual intercourse, or does that in the month of Ramadan. What is due upon them both? He said: 'Upon them both is the expiation, like that upon the one who has sexual intercourse.'

Al-Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And whoever looks at a non-mahram and ejaculates, then a camel is obligatory upon him if he is wealthy, and if he is middle-class, then a cow is upon him, and if he is poor, then a sheep is upon him. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلْكَفَّارَةُ: Expiation or compensation for a ritual violation
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A young camel (specific type of sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for ejaculation without intercourse while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that ejaculation through play (masturbation) while in ihram incurs the same expiation as full sexual intercourse, a ruling derived from the principle of 'tamassuk' (holding fast) to the sanctity of the state. The text further distinguishes the specific sacrificial animals based on the pilgrim's financial capacity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proportional liability. This ruling is particularly significant in distinguishing between minor and major acts of breaking the ihram restrictions.
